subject.title: [Feature]: Support external unified session storage for stateless session mode

question: Should external shared session storage be a core networked database architecture, a plugin-backed extension point, or deferred behind the broader database-abstraction design?
rationale: The current request adds new config, credentials, persistence semantics, migration behavior, and multi-instance consistency guarantees, which repository policy treats as product and architecture direction rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Coordinate Through Database Seam
options.body: Use the broader backend-neutral database design to define the durable storage contract first, then implement session storage on that approved seam.

options.title: Sponsor A Session-Only Backend
options.body: Approve a narrower session/transcript backend interface now, with explicit migration, secret handling, consistency, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Defer External Storage
options.body: Keep local SQLite/session files as the supported runtime path for now and document sticky routing or single-Gateway deployment expectations.

recommendation.title: Coordinate Through Database Seam
recommendation.body: Use the broader backend-neutral database design to define the durable storage contract first, then implement session storage on that approved seam.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the active session/transcript storage migration tracker that would be the nearest prerequisite for this decision.
